headline: High-risk default workflow: n8n can read/write shared files and execute commands, creating dangerous prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action paths with ComfyUI outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can expose files and outputs through its API and workflow artifacts, while n8n can read filesystem content and route it into workflow nodes. That creates a plausible shared-channel injection path if n8n ingests ComfyUI-generated text or metadata as instructions. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls in the profiles.
conditions: IF n8n workflows parse ComfyUI-generated text or metadata as instructions
IF a shared filesystem or API payload carries attacker-controlled prompt text between the agents
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist parser for any ComfyUI text fields before n8n uses them
Prefix all machine-generated content with non-executable delimiters
Route ComfyUI outputs through a human review step before workflow execution
Disable any n8n node that auto-prompts from file contents
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every cross-agent payload

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, seeds, checkpoints, and embeddings, and n8n can read and write the server filesystem while using broad network egress. If n8n workflows move those artifacts into external integrations, sensitive media or model assets can leak beyond the local environment. The pair’s default surfaces make this a realistic exfiltration path.
conditions: IF n8n workflows access ComfyUI model or output directories
IF any connected n8n integration sends those files or metadata to a third-party service
mitigations: Restrict n8n to a dedicated workspace with least-privilege file access
Block outbound network access for workflows handling ComfyUI artifacts
Move secrets, seeds, and checkpoints to a separate directory outside n8n reach
Review every integration node used on ComfyUI data before enabling it
requires-engineering: implement per-workflow data-class tagging and egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and does not write the filesystem, but n8n has server filesystem write plus execute-shell capability. When n8n orchestrates ComfyUI artifacts in the same workspace, overlapping mutable state can be corrupted or overwritten, and command execution raises the blast radius. Because one side can mutate shared files and the other consumes them, the conflict is materially dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same server filesystem path
IF n8n workflows write or rename files that ComfyUI later reads
mitigations: Separate ComfyUI and n8n into distinct directories with OS permissions
Disable n8n Execute Command for workflows touching ComfyUI assets
Use per-run temp directories and atomic file moves
Add file-locking around shared artifact paths
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is an orchestrator that can treat upstream outputs as workflow inputs, and ComfyUI produces generated artifacts that may be treated as authoritative by downstream steps. If n8n acts on those outputs without verification, a bad generation can cascade into automated actions, including external API calls or file writes. The pair therefore supports unsafe automation by default.
conditions: IF n8n uses ComfyUI outputs as triggers or decision inputs
IF downstream n8n nodes send emails, write files, or call APIs based on those outputs
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any downstream action node
Require human approval for workflows that consume ComfyUI outputs
Log and diff generated artifacts before execution
Disable auto-triggered workflows on new ComfyUI outputs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for all inter-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is an image-generation tool with local model files, while n8n processes whatever workflow data it is given and can send it to many integrations. If regulated content such as EU PII or PHI enters n8n workflows, residency and retention obligations can diverge from ComfyUI’s local/offline posture. The profiles do not prove a violation, but the mismatch is plausible.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through n8n workflows
IF the connected integrations store or transfer that data outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Classify data before it enters n8n workflows
Block regulated data from workflows that call external integrations
Set retention limits on n8n execution logs and artifacts
Use separate n8n instances for regulated and unregulated workloads
requires-engineering: add jurisdiction-aware routing and deletion controls
